subject: Livechat streaming delay — mitigation steps and next actions
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finpulse.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Livechat streaming delay — users see token pauses and session timeouts

Hi Mina,

We started seeing elevated latency and intermittent pauses in our livechat sessions around 15:50 EDT today. Customers are reporting tokens arriving in big bursts (several seconds between chunks) and a handful of sessions timed out completely.

Quick details:
- Region: us-east-1
- Model: rdx-8b-stream-v2 (pinned)
- Approx affected sessions: ~120 active connections in the last 30m, ~18 with visible stalls

I've attached logs from one affected websocket session (fp_stream_logs_0614.txt). Can you confirm whether this is on your side (edge/backpressure) or something on our client? We are in a high-traffic window and need a short-term workaround.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Product Operations, FinPulse

Attachment: fp_stream_logs_0614.txt

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finpulse.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Livechat streaming delay — users see token pauses and session timeouts

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. We're investigating now. Initial summary of actions we can take immediately to reduce customer-visible impact (short-term):

1) Switch affected clients to short-polling fallback for 10–20 minutes (non-streamed responses) — this avoids websocket chunking issues and gives a smooth user experience while we triage.
2) Reduce max_tokens to 256 and lower client chunk_size to 64 tokens to reduce sustained open-request pressure.
3) Enable prefix caching on your route (we can flip this on from our side if you prefer).
4) Temporarily route requests to rdx-4b-stable if you can tolerate slightly lower fidelity for the next hour; this has lower memory/KV-cache pressure.

We will also provide a short-runbook for your engineering team to toggle the above items quickly. I'm copying Ben (customer ops) and Laura (incidents/ES escalation) so we can coordinate telemetry and a possible canary rollback.

I'll follow up with a more detailed playbook and a proposed window for a targeted fallback.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:36:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: Re: Livechat streaming delay — quick triage notes

Quick notes from triage:
- Edge telemetry shows increased queued token latency at the us-east-1 proxy layer between 15:42–15:58.
- Several token-emission shards experienced KV cache invalidation after an in-flight model variant swap at 15:44 (orchestration rolled a few nodes with a different quantization profile).
- Autoscaler briefly throttled new request slots while nodes rebalanced; this produced microbursts of queued writes.

Immediate mitigation we recommend:
- Pin FinPulse namespace to the last-stable model instance (avoid variant swap during warm period).
- Disable aggressive node drain for 30m (set drain_time override).
- Hotfix: apply backpressure smoothing patch to the edge proxy (v1.2.3-bp) — ready to deploy, low-risk.

I'll standby to apply the proxy hotfix and to coordinate the pin. Karthik, can you validate whether the autoscaler flags show an unexpected scale-down?

— Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Internal: Re: Livechat streaming delay — quick triage notes

Ben — I pulled the autoscaler logs. There was a short-lived scale-down loop triggered by a readiness probe misclassification (fixed in canary last week but not promoted to stable for this cluster). Scale-down occurred 15:43–15:46 and we see the node pool rejoin around 15:55.

Plan:
- I'll push a config override to stop any scale-downs for FinPulse until 18:00 local.
- Ben, please apply proxy smoothing hotfix (v1.2.3-bp) to us-east-1 edge.
- Mina, confirm with FinPulse whether they want us to flip to the rdx-4b-stable fallback while we patch.

Karthik

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finpulse.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finpulse.com, eng@finpulse.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 17:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Livechat streaming delay — mitigation steps and runbook request

Thanks — we appreciate the quick diagnosis. Please proceed with:
- Pin our namespace to the last-stable model variant immediately.
- Flip the proxy smoothing hotfix.
- As a client-side change we'll drop max_tokens to 256 and reduce chunk_size to 64 for the next 60 minutes (we'll toggle back after you confirm stabilization).

Can you send the runbook steps we should run from our side (exact headers to set, example route toggles, and the recommended websocket keepalive/timeout values)? Also we need an ETA on when you'll share an incident summary and whether this qualifies for a credit under SLA.

Attachment: fp_stream_logs_0614.txt

— Sarah

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finpulse.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 20:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Livechat streaming delay — mitigation steps and runbook request

Hi Sarah — finalizing the runbook and next steps. Summary of actions completed and runbook items for FinPulse: 

Actions we applied (completed 14 Jun, 17:00 EDT):
- Pinned your namespace to last-stable model instance (rdx-8b-stable) to avoid variant swap.
- Deployed edge proxy smoothing patch (v1.2.3-bp) in us-east-1.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive autoscaler scale-down for your namespace until 18:00.

Runbook (client-side toggles you can run immediately):
1) If you have an environment flag for fallbacks, enable non-streaming fallback: set X-Redwood-Fallback: polling; TTL: 120s.
2) Lower request payloads: set max_tokens=256 and client_chunk_size=64.
3) WebSocket keepalive recommendations: set ping interval to 18s, enable TCP keepalive, and set client-side read timeout to 90s (avoid very short timeouts during token bursts).
4) If you need to reduce perceived latency further, temporarily route to rdx-4b-stable by setting model_override=rdx-4b-stable in the request header.
5) Logging: attach the following headers when sending logs to us so we can correlate: X-Request-Id, X-Edge-Shard, X-Model-Variant.

Post-incident items we will deliver by EOD tomorrow (15 Jun):
- Incident summary PDF with timeline and root cause (incident_summary_20270614.pdf).
- Telemetry snapshot (telemetry_snapshot_0614.json) and the logs we used for analysis.
- A proposed customer-facing postmortem meeting time — we suggest Wed 16 Jun, 10:00 EDT.

Regarding SLA credits: we will review the incident under our SLA policy. Laura will follow up with a draft credit offer; we typically provide pro-rated credits for verified service degradation during a covered window.

If anything regresses after the toggles are reverted, please open a high-priority ticket and we'll escalate immediately.

Thanks for partnering on this — talk tomorrow on the PM call if helpful.

— Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_summary_20270614.pdf, telemetry_snapshot_0614.json
